item.title: Re: The Normality
item.content:encoded: crap, that's entirely my bad, I know this is a late reply, but just want to clear the air. I meant to say this situation sucks, not the scp idea. If it's good enough to be an 001 it's obviously a novel and interesting idea, but the situation sucks because the author put so much work into developing this

item.title: Re: The Normality
item.content:encoded:
Hi.
I've read your crit and I wanted to clear some things.
Firstly, I wasn't aware of the Djoric-Dmatix Proposal and its similarity to my idea until now. Thank you for that.
Secondly, while your concern about them being similar are true, I think they are different in essence:
1.) The Djoric-Dmatix Proposal, or the thirty-six, are somewhat aware of what they are capable of, and are part of something huge. However, the normality is just an average person, who lives an average life not knowing what he is and what he could do, and with no part of something grandiose.

2.) The normality does not influence anomalies over a large area, just that which is under his observation or could potentially affect his normal life. This shows that if he was left alone, he would not have affected the foundation or anything at all, and even now, with proper precaution, could be controlled, unlike the thirty-six

3.) The Thirty-Six are contained because they possess a risk of generating large amounts of anomaly upon death, and affecting the entire world. The normality is observed for a different reason, that is, his power to bring equilibrium could wipe out the foundation's existence without actually ending the world, not for threatening reality as we now know it. In other words, the normality is given SCP status not because he is anomalous, but rather because he is normal, a bit too much.

I am sure that you will have more concerns. If so, please do not hesitate to give me your feedback
Thank you

item.title: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
blazerboy69420, while I agree with your assessment of the above critique, please remember to refrain from making personal statements like "I'm not sure you even know what reality anchors are tbh" when addressing another reviewer.

Poiuytree, when providing feedback, you don't necessarily need to tell an author exactly how to edit their concept to improve it, but you should try to provide some sort of viable direction to follow. Can you explain what you as a reader would need to see to be more interested in reading a draft of the concept? For more information on providing critique in this forum, please see this thread: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-9804362/so-you-want-to-be-a-concept-reviewer

item.title: Re: The Normality
item.content:encoded: Yeah telling the guy his idea sucks and that he shouldn't even try to execute the concept is almost, if not crossing the "Don't be a dick" rule. Not to mention this is just straight up poor crit. Similar concepts that exist on the wiki can be executed way differently and end up becoming entirely different scips. That's the equivalent of saying that Atonement is ripping off Dr. Manhattan because of the 'experiment-gone-wrong' shtick and the Darkbody being super powerful. You're not really telling them how to improve the concept either besides "lol just make it different or something". I'm not sure you even know what reality anchors are tbh. They forcibly bend reality back to equilibrium when an anomaly that screws with humes pop up (though how that's achieved is up for interpretation), they don't strip the anomalous abilities of an anomaly. Be better man.

item.title: Re: The Normality
item.content:encoded: This sucks cause it sounds like you've put a great deal of effort into thinking it out, but this is almost exactly an scp we already have, an 001 in fact. the Djoric-Dmatix proposal is about 36 people who alter scps, which most often winds up in the scps being completely disabled. While it's not always disabled, it is the most often effect they cause. If you can somehow make it different enough, that would be good, but I'm worried that the idea may just have to be abandoned due to similarity.

item.title: The Normality
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The most average man in the world, who's everything (height, weight, general routine, you name it) is very normal, has the unconscious power to remove the abnormal properties of every anomaly he comes across temporarily, if not erase it completely, provided that they should remain under his observable range or presence. Doesn't realize his powers, since every anomalous event is forcibly made to look normal to him.

Central Narrative: The Normality was found by accident when one of the SCP broke containment and coincidentally ran into him, henceforth being neutralized and re-secured. At first the foundation takes an interest in him, trying to recruit him since he could be a key to neutralizing all anomaly.

However, none of the foundation members were able to approach him due to his nature, and they decided instead to use him indirectly, by testing and putting forward SCPs to be erased. However, when they planned on erasing a keter class using him, it results in the foundation almost collapsing, since the foundation itself could be considered an anomaly, and anything that could affect his normal life gets influenced by his ability.

After closely preventing that, further testing and attempts to erase anomalies was stopped, because every anomaly he encounters afterwards carries the risk of letting the foundation come under his influence. Hence he was given SCP status, put under watch, and was prevented from coming in contact with anything abnormal.

Hooks: SCP is famous for trying to keep the most anomalous in check. It would interest both new and old fans to see how they would try to deal with the opposite. Also, the foundation's primary goal is to preserve reality and order. The normality could show an outlook on when moving towards that very goal can be disastrous.

Additional notes: This is my first SCP. Please tell me how may I improve on this, if any.
